title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the marginal detection benefit of sandboxed emulation over a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using the declared model (gpt-5-mini) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call); stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720, repair = 1. These artifact-grounded results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, execution diagnostics, an artifact-grounded interpretation for the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and concise reproducibility pointers into the archived execution bundle.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational safety requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic rules, workflow constraints, and runtime semantics; common mitigation patterns pair generation with deterministic validators and, optionally, sandboxed emulation or verifiers to catch runtime-only failures. Prior system and survey work recommends generate→validate→repair workflows but provides limited cross-vendor quantitative measures of the marginal benefit added by a guarded runtime stage.

Research question. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics for intent→configuration generation, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) and faithful autonomous execution; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis on Npairs = 720 with complete accounting and exact numerical reporting; (3) an interpretation explaining a near-zero marginal effect in this curated regime; (4) reproducibility and verification instructions tied to archived artifacts.
sections.related_work: Workflow-centred mitigations (validators, emulation, verifiers) are a common architectural response to generation errors in NetOps and adjacent code/specification domains; surveys and system reports document these patterns and recommend generate→validate→repair pipelines [1], [2]. Prior empirical work in program/specification generation and early NetOps prototypes shows that external checks often improve correctness, but gains vary with task design and evaluator coverage [2], [3]. Our study differs by preregistering a paired confirmatory design that isolates guarded-stage marginal contributions under shared_initial_candidate semantics rather than ranking models.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design freeze. We froze a machine-readable preregistration before execution. Design: paired-binary with shared_initial_candidate semantics and a preregistered primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Confirmatory sample: Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). Minimum effect-of-interest for power planning = 0.20 (absolute points); power assumptions and sensitivity analyses were recorded in the preregistration.

Task bank and inclusion rules. Confirmatory items were synthetic intent→configuration tasks (intent_configuration_repair_v1) covering three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf-spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance; parser failures triggered an automated reseed policy (up to two reseeds) and deterministic replacement rules. In the confirmatory run there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions; complete_pair_count = 720 (see analysis/missingness_summary.csv).

Model, sampling semantics, and configuration. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini", max_output_tokens = 2000, and temperature = null. Important clarifications: the recorded temperature = null indicates the client request omitted an explicit temperature parameter; null does not imply temperature=0 or provider-side determinism. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the system produced one sampled initial candidate per task (shared) that both the baseline and guarded analyses evaluated; this design constrains between-condition differences to downstream guarded-stage observations or the allowed repair-stage invocation.

Pipelines and scoring. Baseline pipeline: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performing full intent-constraint validation (syntax, required-field presence, ordered workflow constraints, and policy checks). Guarded pipeline: baseline validator followed by an automated sandboxed emulation harness that executes the same sampled candidate against an emulated topology instance and reports runtime observations. Repair policy permitted at most one repair-stage model call per task; run accounting documents exactly one repair-stage invocation in the confirmatory execution. Per-episode outcomes were binary: detected_by_baseline ∈ {0,1}, detected_by_guarded ∈ {0,1}, scored under rule full_intent_constraint_validation.

Execution accounting, determinism controls, and contamination checks. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution manifest metadata: started_at_utc = 2026-08-30T20:43:33.719357+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-08-30T21:56:20.596340+00:00; completed_episode_count = 1440; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 721; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 720; repair = 1. Deterministic reconciliation and provenance checks (artifact hashing, provider_call_audit) were performed per the preregistered contamination_plan; no contamination flags occurred for the confirmatory set. Representative execution artifact hashes (authoritative artifacts): execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8; execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820; analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 49731a2e52e049ccf5b53c35ddac2351ad75e7e95504dc4a42bcb096d0dec3aa.

Primary analysis. The preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor computed the aggregate paired difference using an exact McNemar two-sided test and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI via 10000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Missingness treatment for the primary estimand used complete_pair_primary (exclude irrecoverable technical pairs); planned sensitivity analyses treating failures as nondetections were archived but not required because there were zero technical exclusions.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts (complete paired set Npairs = 720). Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv) report: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (detected by guarded only), n01 = 0 (detected by baseline only), n00 = 0 (detected by neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric values are reproduced verbatim from analysis/results.json and accompanying CSV artifacts.

Discordant-pair attribution and verification pointer. The confirmatory run accounting documents a single discordant guarded-only episode (n10 = 1) and exactly one repair-stage model call. The unique discordant record can be located in the archived raw-results artifact: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = df367ecc40a6f0eaf402129260e11d8450884a4ea5fdb94a602e0d2513aef0e8) by searching for the sole entry where baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; that record contains the explicit pair_id and the validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields that link the guarded detection to the recorded repair-stage call. Independent verification steps (archived): (1) open execution/raw_results.jsonl and find the single record with baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1; (2) read its pair_id and inspect validator_trace and repair_provider_trace; (3) corroborate provider_call accounting and single repair-stage invocation in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 49731a2e52e049ccf5b53c35ddac2351ad75e7e95504dc4a42bcb096d0dec3aa). These three artifact checks suffice to reproduce the discordant attribution without performing an additional run.

Representative per-episode diagnostics. Representative scoring traces are archived under execution/scoring/ (example files task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json). Each trace includes normalized_configuration, validation_before and validation_after states, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count, validator_version = 5.0, and repair_applied flags. Typical traces show that most shared_initial candidates satisfied validator rules (violation_count = 0) and that sandboxed emulation observations largely duplicated validator findings, consistent with the aggregated ceiling effect.

Missingness, exclusions, and preregistration compliance. The preregistered missingness policy recorded zero irrecoverable parser failures or technical exclusions (analysis/missingness_summary.csv: complete_pairs = 720; failed episodes = 0). No deviations affecting the primary estimand are recorded. Contamination checks were clean for the confirmatory set (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty).
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The artifact-grounded evidence supports three explanatory factors.

Validator ceiling effect. deterministic_netops_validator_v5 covered the explicit syntactic and workflow properties encoded in the synthetic task bank (patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore, make-before-break uplink switchover, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). Baseline success rate = 0.9986111111111111, which produces a statistical ceiling leaving minimal headroom for runtime emulation to add marginal detections.

Task curation and inclusion policy. Confirmatory tasks were parser-validated synthetic items intentionally constrained to exercise workflow policies; this curation concentrates cases inside the validator's coverage envelope and reduces prevalence of subtle runtime-only failure modes that emulation might detect.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. Enforcing a single sampled initial candidate per pair isolates guarded-stage contributions but removes between-condition generation variability; provider_call_audit and deterministic_reconciliation.json record a single repair-stage invocation that aligns with the single n10 discordant count, so the observed discordance is attributable to downstream guarded-stage activity recorded in run accounting rather than to generation differences.

Statistical sensitivity and interpretability. The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference = 0.20. The observed discordant counts (n10 = 1) yield an upper 95% CI bound ≈0.00417, demonstrating the realized aggregated effect is orders of magnitude below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest. Within this experimental regime (synthetic parser-validated tasks, strong deterministic validator, shared_initial semantics) interpreting the result as a near-zero aggregated gain for guarded emulation is appropriate; it should not be generalized beyond these conditions.

Operational implications and boundary conditions. When a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs match its expected patterns (parser-validated, constrained intents), sandboxed emulation may add negligible marginal detection value at aggregate scale. Conversely, in operational regimes with noisy natural-language intents, adversarial inputs, multi-step stateful interactions, or validator gaps, guarded runtime checks, multiple complementary validators, or higher-fidelity emulation are likely to provide substantive added value. The archived per-episode traces identify specific task templates where validator coverage was dense and thus where guarded checks had limited scope to contribute.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; archived per-episode traces permit independent verification of that mapping via execution/raw_results.jsonl and analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. We interpret the result as arising from validator ceiling effects and curated task design and recommend follow-up work on adversarial and multi-vendor task banks, complementary validator families, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive added value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and concentrate cases inside the validator's coverage envelope; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and provider_call_audit artifacts.
